entities.summary: Lolita, a novel by Vladimir Nabokov, is a 1955 text that explores themes of desire, identity, and morality in the Global context. Created by Vladimir Nabokov, c. 1950, Lolita is a Contemporary work that has had significant effects on the Literary genre. The novel's protagonist, Humbert Humbert, is a key figure associated with pedophilia and has been the subject of controversy and debate. Lolita's legacy can be seen in its influence on the development of Postmodern literature and its exploration of the complexities of human desire. The novel has been translated into numerous languages and has sold millions of copies worldwide. Lolita's significanceScore is 7, reflecting its regional impact on the Literary genre. Its significanceNarrative is that Lolita has had a lasting impact on the way authors explore themes of desire and morality. Its significanceCategory is regional, reflecting its influence on the development of Postmodern literature.
